title: Canary contingency matrix and comms scripts (working)
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects a compact contingency matrix (decision table) for canary activations + ready-to-send communications for each outcome. The goal is to reduce cognitive load during early-stage rollouts and give stewards a one-page actionable script when a canary deviates from expectations.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to feature rollouts that modify inference models, routing policies, safety filters, or cost controls (e.g., quantization changes, KV cache policy tweaks, routing weight shifts).
- Canary window defaults: 1 hour for latency/cost signal checks, 24 hours for quality/behavior signals. Can be shortened for high-risk slices.
- Signals covered: latency P50/P95/P99, token cost per call, error rate (5xx), semantic quality regressions (prompt-level evals), user-facing correctness (manual review), safety triggers (policy hits), and unusual distribution shifts (input deviance).

How to use this doc:
1) Before activation: fill the top row (canary id, hypothesis, key metrics, baseline values) and pin contact names.
2) During canary: monitor the quick table (green/amber/red) and follow the matching row in the contingency matrix. Communications block contains short Slack templates and customer-facing lines where relevant.
3) After resolution: paste final notes into the canary ticket and mark follow-ups.

Quick checklist (prep)
- Owner assigned, oncall informed, comms channels verified (channel: #rollouts, escalation: #sre-pager).
- Synthetic probes configured for canary slice.
- Evaluation harness: 50 labeled prompts (smoke set) with expected outputs and automated diff baseline.
- Rollback/reversion playbook validated in staging (can restore model vN-1 within X minutes).

Contingency matrix (decision table):
Columns: Trigger | Severity | Immediate action (first 15m) | Who to notify | Follow-up action (next 1-24h) | Comms script

1) Trigger: Latency P95 > baseline + 200ms for > 5 minutes
Severity: Medium
Immediate action: Move canary traffic to lower-weight bucket (reduce exposure by 70%), enable temporary rate-limit throttle, collect traces
Who: SRE lead, runtime engineer, product steward
Follow-up: Investigate kernel selection, warm caches, consider model variant with shorter context; if unresolved in 60m, rollback to previous model
Comms script (internal): "Canary {{id}}: sustained P95 spike +200ms. Reduced exposure to 30% and enabled throttles. Tracing available at <link>. Paging SRE./ Will update in 15m"
Comms script (customer-facing if customer-facing traffic affected): "We detected increased response latency for a small subset of requests; we've temporarily reduced exposure while we investigate. No action required from you; we'll follow up shortly."

2) Trigger: Error rate (5xx) > baseline * 3 or absolute > 0.5% for > 5 minutes
Severity: High
Immediate action: Kill canary traffic (0% exposure), switch traffic to fallback model/region, open incident in PagerDuty
Who: SRE oncall, runtime, product PM, CS lead (if customer impact)
Follow-up: Root cause analysis, hotfix or rollback, postmortem within 72h
Comms script (internal): "High error rate on canary {{id}}. Cut to 0% and failed over. Incident channel: <pd-link>. Owning SRE: @name."
Comms script (external): "We observed an elevated error rate for some requests and have reverted to the prior service configuration to maintain availability. Sorry for the disruption; we'll share details after analysis."

3) Trigger: Semantic regression on smoke set (automated diffs exceed threshold)
Severity: Medium-High (context dependent)
Immediate action: Pause further rollout; triage with applied-ML and product; run expanded eval suite (500 prompts)
Who: Applied ML, product steward, stewarded reviewers
Follow-up: Decide to proceed with narrower slice, tweak prompt templates, or rollback if quality gap unacceptable
Comms script (internal): "Canary {{id}} shows semantic delta > threshold on smoke set. Paused rollout. Triage with applied-ML. Eval job: <ci-link>"
Comms script (external, if customers using preview): "We've paused the expanded preview while our models undergo additional checks to ensure response quality. No action required from you."

4) Trigger: Safety policy hits spike or new hallucination class observed
Severity: Critical
Immediate action: Immediately stop canary, notify Safety and Legal, engage incident channel, collect examples (store in secure bucket)
Who: Safety lead, Legal oncall, product steward, CS if customer-facing
Follow-up: Deep investigation, potential recall of change, formal incident and legal review, notify customers if necessary
Comms script (internal): "SAFETY: urgent stop. Canary {{id}} produced safety violations. Samples at <secure-link>. Paging Safety and Legal."
Comms script (external tentative): "We identified content that does not meet our safety standards during a limited rollout. We have paused the deployment and are investigating. We will reach out if any customer action is needed."

5) Trigger: Cost per token increases > 20% and sustained for > 2h
Severity: Low-Medium
Immediate action: Throttle background traffic, limit maximum tokens per call, roll back cost-intensive config (e.g., remove heavy reranker)
Who: Product steward, finance ops, runtime engineer
Follow-up: Re-evaluate costing model and rollout gating thresholds; update Optimize suggestions
Comms script (internal): "Cost spike observed on canary {{id}}. Limiting token cap and disabling optional reranker for canary traffic."

Human gates and decision rubric
- Green: All signals within ±5% of baseline or within defined acceptable delta. Proceed with planned exposure ramp.
- Amber: One or two signals outside thresholds but non-critical (latency or cost). Pause ramp, reduce exposure, require a short retrospective checkpoint (owner + SRE) before continuing.
- Red: Safety violations, high error rate, or multiple severe quality regressions. Immediate stop and rollback.

Who signs off to ramp from 30% -> 60% exposure?
- Required: Product steward, SRE owner, Applied ML rep (for model changes). If customer traffic included, CS lead signs off for communication plan.

Escalation timings and SLAs during canary
- First 5 minutes: owner posts status to #rollouts and pings SRE oncall.
- 15 minutes: if trigger unresolved and severity >= medium, page primary SRE and product manager.
- 60 minutes: if unresolved, execute rollback unless an explicit 'hold' is declared with rationale and mitigation plan.

Comms templates (shortened, copy/paste)
- Internal status update (1-liner): "Canary {{id}} | status: RED/AMBER/GREEN | action taken: [reduced|paused|reverted] | next update T+15m | traces: <link>"
- Customer-facing brief (email/CS): "Hi [Customer], we briefly rolled a change that affected a subset of traffic and observed [latency/errors/quality drift]. We've reverted that change for now and will share a postmortem. Apologies for any disruption. (account rep: @name)"
- Post-rollback note (channel): "Canary {{id}} rolled back at T+{{min}}. Root cause investigation started; linking artifacts: <links>. Follow-ups assigned: @names."

Simulated rehearsals and drills (ops hygiene)
- Quarterly tabletop where we inject a synthetic P95 spike and walk through the contingency matrix. Owner: SRE lead.
- Bi-weekly smoke replays: run the 50-prompt harness against the canary variant and baseline; compare diffs, log any drift.
- Blameless postmortem template: timeline, detection lead, decision log, follow-ups, economic impact estimate.

Open questions / TODOs
- Add a standard format for 'acceptance delta' per model family (e.g., chat LLM vs. reranker).
- Automate Slack templates via the console so steward can click 'notify customers' and auto-fill account lists.
- Link the canary ticket to the rollout run in the Console (one-click).

Appendix: quick owner checklist (during incident)
1) Snapshot logs and traces (link)
2) Collect 10 representative examples (for safety/quality) and upload to secure artifact store
3) Post update to #rollouts (1-line) and notify SRE oncall
4) If stopping, flip traffic and confirm metrics stabilize at prior baseline
5) Schedule postmortem and assign follow-ups

Notes on tone and comms: keep customer language concise, empathetic, and action-oriented. Avoid technical jargon in customer-facing messages; internal messages should contain links to artifacts and brief next steps.

End of doc.
